name: TN-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+13 partisan lean in a Republican-leaning state
Garrett's large fundraising advantage over Croley
Prediction markets price Republican win near 95%
Open seat removes incumbent risk but no polling available
model.rationale: The R+13 district lean, Garrett's roughly 67-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Republican win at about 95% all point the same way, with no polling or ratings suggesting a competitive race. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based expectation of a double-digit Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Democrat within single digits, or a major scandal involving Garrett, would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John Rose (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Tennessee's 6th District is an open seat after Republican John Rose left the race to run for governor. The district leans Republican by about 13 points, and Republican nominee Johnny Garrett enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $2.4 million to Democrat Mike Croley's $35,000, who reports minimal cash on hand. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 95 percent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and money. Croley would need an unusual environment shift to close a double-digit structural gap. The race is rated Safe Republican, with modest uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
